// - Repeating digits (e.g., 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA)
// - Alternating pairs (e.g., 0x8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F8F)
// - Incremental sequences (e.g., 0x20202020202020202020202020202020)
// These patterns emerge because we're dealing with powers of 2 in a 64-bit space,
// which creates specific bit patterns rather than random combinations.
// The patterns we see are determined by the mathematical properties of
// exponentiation in binary arithmetic.
// Values cycle through a fixed set of hex patterns
// Pattern continues up to 200000
// Each block of 64 numbers follows the same sequence
// Example: 799-863, 863-927, 927-991, etc. all follow same pattern
